archive.notes: git archive of the base commit filtered by construction/filter_tar.py: the 16 excised files removed; tests/assets/rrd (558 MB, includes the checked-in snippet reference recordings), tests/assets/gaussian_splats, tests/python, examples/python, examples/notebook, rerun_notebook, rerun_js, viewer snapshot PNGs (crates/**/tests/snapshots and tests/rust/re_integration_test/tests/snapshots, git-lfs) and unused video clips dropped. Every Cargo workspace member (crates/**, docs/snippets, examples/rust/*, rerun_py, run_wasm, tests/rust/*) is kept so `cargo fetch/build --locked` can load the workspace; filter_tar.py asserts that no member manifest is dropped (the first archive dropped tests/rust and broke the rust-build stage). git-lfs smudged the two AV1 clips and the mcap that snippets read.

oracle.reference: Rust snippets (docs/snippets/all/**/*.rs, built as the `snippets` crate at the same commit) produce the baseline .rrd files at verifier image build; `rerun rrd compare --unordered --ignore-chunks-without-components` (rerun-cli built at the same commit, no viewer) compares the C++ output, exactly as docs/snippets/compare_snippet_output.py --no-py does upstream. Plus rerun_cpp/tests (Catch2 v3.4.0, 45 test cases) restored from pristine.
oracle.python_baseline: Not used. The Python SDK wheel would require building rerun_py (maturin + full Rust build); upstream uses Rust as the baseline whenever Rust runs, and every C++-runnable snippet has a runnable Rust sibling, so dropping Python loses zero comparisons.

contamination.notes: The excised code is public in rerun-io/rerun (history since 2023, stable since 0.31). Not interface-shifted: headers, tests and snippets are upstream-verbatim so generated code and the snippet corpus keep compiling. Suitable for RL data; weak for headroom claims. Mitigations available: interface-shift the private members (e.g. rename detail::to_rr_string, change ComponentBatch::to_c_ffi_struct to return a struct) at the cost of regenerating snippets/tests; or switch to a newer commit at construction time.

horizon.proxy: 16 files, ~1060 lines to write across 13 headers' worth of declarations; three interacting boundaries (Arrow C Data Interface export/ownership, rerun_c C ABI incl. error codes and special handles, C++ error-handling semantics incl. strict mode and log handlers); verified by 45 unit test cases and 104 cross-language differential comparisons; build cycle 2-20 minutes.
